slides.h: Why hotel beds look like that.
slides.dek: Four moves housekeeping makes that most bedrooms skip.

slides.h: The linen is plain and white.
body: Hotels standardised on white because it survives industrial washing. The side effect is the point.
White bedding reads crisp and intentional in any room, under any light, forever.

slides.h: The duvet runs one size up.
body: A king duvet on a queen bed drops the sides low and hides the mattress line.
That overhang is most of the plush the eye remembers from a hotel room.

slides.h: One folded layer at the foot.
body: A coverlet or throw folded in thirds across the foot of the bed.
It adds the single line of weight and texture the white field needs.

slides.h: Pillows stack by size, back to front.
body: Sleepers at the back, standards in front, one lumbar at most.
Even numbers keep the stack calm. Odd cushions are where hotel turns hostel.

slides.h: Save this for the next linen change.
